Find the best blend of language models

Source: R/ai-coverage.R
blend_llms.Rd

Searches the blend weights for an synthetic_coverage() result again, for example with a finer grid or without holding out attempts. The recipe with the highest mean overlap on the attempts it is chosen on wins; with holdout, it is chosen on the first half of the attempts and reported on the second half.

Usage

blend_llms(x, holdout = NULL, step = 0.05, seed = 1)

Arguments

x

an mv_coverage object from synthetic_coverage().

holdout

choose on half of the attempts and report on the other half? NULL does so when every model has four or more attempts.

step

grid step for the weights (coarser steps are used for more than six models).

seed

random seed for the pooled sample behind the blend's structure.

Value

x with a "Best Blend" row in summary, its cells and attempts added, and blend: A list with weights (a named vector), recipe (text), train and test (the attempts used) and in_sample (the mean overlap on the attempts the recipe was chosen on).

See also

synthetic_coverage(), gg_coverage()

Examples

set.seed(1)
a <- matrix(rlnorm(8, 0.2, 0.3)); d <- matrix(rnorm(8))
real <- as.data.frame(simdata(a, d, 600, itemtype = "dich"))
llm <- function(mu, s) lapply(1:4, function(i) as.data.frame(
  simdata(a, d, 150, itemtype = "dich", Theta = matrix(rnorm(150, mu, s)))))
cov <- synthetic_coverage(list(A = llm(0.8, 0.7), B = llm(-0.6, 0.9)), real,
                          blend = FALSE)
blend_llms(cov, holdout = FALSE)$blend$recipe
#> [1] "50% A + 50% B"
